articles.title: Oh, how we wish the haze choking South-East Asia was just fog
articles.dek: At last, over the weekend, the “haze” began to subside over Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, where I live. For nearly two months, the noxious air emanating from fires, mainly on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, had caused about 300,000 to suffer respiratory illness in Indonesia and led to a 260 per cent surge in asthma cases in Malaysia. As this blight on daily life lifted in parts of the region, two thoughts struck me: first, how unaware so many are in other parts of the world about what the haze actually is, and second, how little serious attention it has been given in most international news.

articles.title: Column: Hawaii’s relationship economy is our edge in the age of AI
articles.dek: In Hawaii, business is almost always intertwined with personal; we value relationships above transactions. The client you’re meeting this week may well be your child’s soccer coach, your kumu hula, or a coworker’s brother. This interconnectedness and relational aspect of our community is more than a charming sidenote — it’s our uniquely human way of doing business in Hawaii and it’s a distinctive form of economics. Trust capital, built and strengthened through human relationships, lowers the cost of doing business, and it’s something the rest of the world can’t easily copy.
